record.ROLE_TEXT:
Director of Operations, North America

**About Us:**

We are committed to finding smart solutions that enable an intelligent and seamless world. Our success as a world-class leader in technology has evolved from humble beginnings. In 1896, the enterprising father and son team of A.J. and George A. Briggs partnered with S.A. Buffington, a Chicago lawyer, to establish Chicago Telephone Supply Company (later to become CTS).

Today, CTS is a leading designer and manufacturer of sensors, actuators, and electronic components for suppliers and original equipment manufacturers. We have over 20 locations in 12 countries and more than 3,500 employees. Our innovative sensing, connectivity, and motion solutions offer a diverse range of products across diversified end markets including transportation, medical, aerospace and defense, and industrial. We are at the forefront of supporting innovating life-changing technology, focusing on quality to keep people safe, healthy, and happy.

**Position Summary**

The Operations Director, North America provides strategic and operational leadership for the regional manufacturing network, ensuring safe, compliant, cost-effective, and customer-focused execution across assigned sites. This position requires a hands-on, execution-focused leader who can standardize operating processes, improve performance variability across sites, coach plant leadership teams, and convert strategic business priorities into measurable operational and financial results. This role is accountable for safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, productivity, customer responsiveness, capital execution, and people development across the North America plants.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the North America manufacturing operations network, establishing clear priorities, standard work, operating cadences, and performance expectations across assigned sites.
* Own regional operational performance and operational excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, productivity, customer responsiveness, and employee engagement metrics.
* Partner with business unit leadership, plant managers, supply chain, quality, engineering, finance, HR, and commercial teams to align operating plans with customer demand and business objectives.
* Establish and reinforce standardized operating processes across the region while allowing appropriate site-level flexibility based on product, customer, and regulatory requirements.
* Drive a disciplined daily, weekly, and monthly management system to review performance, identify gaps, assign accountability, and ensure timely corrective actions.
* Translate operational actions into financial outcomes by improving margin performance, controlling costs, optimizing resources, and partnering with finance on budgeting and forecasting.
* Provide leadership, coaching, and development for plant managers and site leadership teams, building a strong succession pipeline and culture of accountability.
* Champion a zero-harm safety culture and ensure compliance with company EHS standards and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Ensure customer requirements are met or exceeded, including on-time delivery, responsiveness, quality performance, and timely resolution of escalations.
* Lead continuous improvement and Lean deployment across the region, including visual management, standard work, 5S, value stream improvement, structured problem solving, and waste reduction.
* Reduce performance variability between sites by deploying common metrics, operating reviews, best-practice sharing, and targeted improvement plans.
* Drive structural cost improvement through labor efficiency, material yield, scrap reduction, inventory optimization, manufacturing productivity, and capacity utilization.
* Review and approve capital project proposals, support business cases, and ensure approved capital expenditures are implemented on time, on budget, and with expected returns.
* Support digital manufacturing, automation, data

record.ROLE_TEXT:
**Role Description**
The Vice President of Quality Assurance is a senior, full-time remote role responsible for leading the quality vision, strategy, and execution across Allianz Trade’s operations. This position oversees the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of quality assurance frameworks, policies, and procedures to ensure consistent service delivery and compliance with internal standards and external regulations. Day-to-day tasks include directing quality audits, monitoring quality performance metrics, identifying root causes of issues, and driving corrective and preventive actions in partnership with cross-functional leaders. The role involves collaborating with operations, technology, compliance, and risk management teams to embed quality best practices into processes, systems, and customer interactions. The Vice President will also guide and mentor quality teams, manage departmental budgets, and report on quality objectives, outcomes, and strategic initiatives to executive leadership.

**Qualifications**

* Strong background in Quality Assurance and Quality Control, with demonstrated experience designing and leading enterprise-wide quality programs.
* Expertise in Quality Management and Quality Auditing, including setting performance standards, conducting audits, and implementing continuous improvement initiatives.
* Solid understanding of Regulatory Requirements relevant to financial services or insurance, with the ability to translate regulatory expectations into practical quality controls.
* Proven leadership experience in senior quality or operational roles, including managing teams, influencing stakeholders, and driving change across complex organizations.
* Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with proficiency in using data and metrics to evaluate performance and prioritize improvements.
* Strong communication and collaboration abilities, including presenting to executive audiences and partnering effectively with global and cross-functional teams in a remote environment.
* Relevant academic background, such as a bachelor’s or master’s degree in business, operations, engineering, quality management, or a related field; professional certifications (e.g., Six Sigma, ISO, CQE/CQA) are a plus.
* Experience within insurance, financial services, or risk management industries is highly beneficial, along with familiarity with digital tools and enterprise quality systems.

1.0 FTE Full time Day - 08 Hour R2655441 Hybrid 108400006 SC Administration Business & Administration PALO ALTO, 1840 Embarcadero, California
 
 
If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.
 
 
Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)
 
 
**This is a Stanford Health Care job.**
**A Brief Overview**
The Director of Supply Chain Operational Excellence is a senior leadership role driving enterprise‑wide efficiency, innovation, and transformation across a Gartner top‑2 ranked healthcare supply chain. With system‑wide influence and a seat at the leadership table, this role partners closely with the Chief Supply Chain Officer and Vice President of Strategic Initiatives to turn strategy into measurable results. The ideal candidate combines healthcare supply chain expertise with strong program management skills and a passion for developing people, leading change, and delivering measurable, enterprise‑wide impact.
 
 
**Locations**
Stanford Health Care
 
 
**What You Will Do**

* Maintain continuous alignment with defined organizational and departmental strategic business objectives in conjunction with leadership.
* Direct and ensure the efficient operation of day-to-day activities of the team and ensure competency of all staff.
* Supports and partners on Change Management, Training and Communications activities as needed for effective performance improvement and project management.
* Act in an advisory capacity to all Supply Chain divisions, programs, staff and leaders.
* Provide expertise, guidance and training on Performance Improvement and Project Management best practices.
* Apply LEAN/Six Sigma principles and methods to identify waste reduction and performance optimization opportunities across Supply Chain operations.
* Implement, oversee and continuously improve Supply Chain systems, processes and standard work to drive the efficient management of operations across Logistics, Sourcing, Procurement, Business Office, Resiliency, Sustainability, Data Management and other functions.
* Build, develop and grow business relationships with Supply Chain’s key stakeholders and partners including but not limited to the Interventional Platform, A/P, Pharmacy, and IT.
* Lead cross-departmental initiatives, establishing strong governance, communication, and accountability to deliver progress measurable through mutually agreed KPIs.
* Align and collaborate with the enterprise Performance Improvement team and Stanford Operating System (SOS).
* Lead the implementation of programs and/or projects as assigned by the Administrative Director.

**Education Qualifications**

* Requires a Bachelor’s degree in a work-related discipline/field from an accredited college or university.
* Relevant experience in lieu of degree may be considered. Relevant experience in lieu of degree is in addition to the experience requirements for this position.

**Experience Qualifications**

* Seven (7) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience.

**Required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities**

* Must have strong leadership and interpersonal skills and be effective at people management including the ability to delegate assignments and share decision-making with team members and direct reports as appropriate.

record.ROLE_TEXT:
**Job Description**
Be part of the global Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) Engineering leadership team driving factory improvements, product improvements for producibility and cost savings, manufacturing technology implementation, and new product development for Honeywell Aerospace.
 
 
We are hiring a Sr Director to lead the global ISC Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) team for New Product Introduction (NPI) supporting programs across the Aerospace portfolio.
 
 
In this role, you will leverage your extensive product development experience and leadership skills. You will drive continuous improvement to develop new products, processes, and standards in support of the organization's business strategies with a direct impact on development program success. You will develop strategy, hold teams accountable and deliver high impact business results.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Deliver NPI program objectives including product producibility, design-to-cost (DTC) targets, production readiness, and customer quality.
* Operate as a change agent to embed producibility into our core design processes.
* Build Employee Engagement and Skills through the development of standard work, clear roles and responsibilities, and effective training programs.
* Design and develop Management Operating Systems to ensure effective team operations, driving results to program and department objectives.
* Work closely with the SBU engineering team, Program Management, and ISC leaders to build cross-organizational alignment

**Qualifications**
**YOU MUST HAVE**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
* 8 years of experience in New Product Development
* Knowledge of manufacturing processes
* Experience working with suppliers on technical issues
* Track record of managing multiple projects with demonstrated results on a macro scale
* Experience leading a team with direct line reporting responsibility
* Abitlity to travel 30%

**Us Person Requirements**
Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.
 
 
**WE VALUE**

* Advanced degree in engineering or business
* Exceptional data analysis and communication skills
* Willingness to raise standards each year to drive organizational excellence
* Ability to make sound and timely judgments in ambiguous environment
* Ability to convey subtle or complex messages clearly, as appropriate for the topic and audience.
* Diverse and global teaming and collaboration
* Balance between demand and capacity when establishing priorities for the organization.

**For Mn Candidates**
The annual base salary range for this position is $238,000-$297,000. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.
 
 
This position is incentive eligible.
 
 
**Benefits**
Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:
 
 

* Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage
* 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
* Employee assistance program and educational assistance
* Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
* Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/

Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with the**Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award**, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

At Crème de la Crème, learning comes alive like nowhere else. Our centers are places that never stand still because kids never do. And when you join us, you’ll become part of that magic—making a memorable impact on young learners and their families every day. In our wow-worthy world of learning, your talents will be the catalyst for creating child care experiences you've never imagined. You’ll link arms with other exceptional humans who care as much about helping kids reach their highest potential as you do—and you’ll know that your work matters.

* As the Crème School Director of Education and Quality, you will 
 + Lead and develop teachers to ensure curriculum alignment with best practices, state standards, and the individual needs of children.
 + Facilitate training and implementation of our comprehensive and developmentally appropriate curriculum for early childhood education.
 + Provide transformative leadership in the field of early childhood education, staying informed about current trends, research, and best practices.
 + Develop a culture of continuous learning and professional development while leading the teaching staff.
 + Establish and maintain high-quality standards for early childhood education program
 + Conduct regular assessments, evaluations, and audits to ensure compliance with Crème standards and licensing requirements
 + Provide guidance and support to teaching staff, promoting a positive and collaborative work environment. In partnership with the Executive Director, host professional development programs to enhance educators' skills and knowledge.
 + Cultivate positive relationships with teachers and parents, involving them in their child's education and development.
 + Collaborate with the community to enhance the educational experience and promote your school within the community.
 + Assist as needed in daily school operations, at times including direct supervision of children
 + Apply data-driven insights to assess program effectiveness, implement strategies to address identified areas of improvement, fostering a culture of continuous quality enhancement.
* Qualifications:
* + Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, Education Administration, or a related field. (preferred)
 + Meet state specific credentials / guidelines for the role
 + At least one year leadership experience in early childhood education or a related field
 + Proven understanding of early childhood development, educational best practices, and program administration.
 + Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
 + Outstanding customer service skills, strong organizational skills, and multi-task and handle multiple situations optimally.

About Epirus 

 Epirus is a high-growth technology company developing solid-state, software-defined directed energy systems that enable unprecedented counter-electronics effects and power management solutions to optimize power efficiency in defense and commercial applications. With a constant emphasis on innovation, we are redefining the future of power to bring tomorrow’s capabilities to life, today. And that’s just the beginning. 

 Job Summary 

 Epirus is seeking a strategic, execution-driven Senior Director of Field Operations & Sustainment (FOS) to lead our global customer-facing deployment, support, and validation operations. As a pioneer in software-defined, high-power microwave (HPM) national security solutions—including our flagship Leonidas platform—we are scaling rapidly to support U.S. Department of Defense (DoD), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and international allied customers. 

 High visibility role, reporting into Chief Operating Officer (COO), this role oversees the end-to-end post-manufacturing lifecycle, serving as Epirus’s Deployment Coordinator while leading our five core operational pillars: Field System Readiness & Deployment, Field Service & Technical Operations, Systems Training & Documentation, Global Delivery & Parts Logistics, and Customer Demonstration & Drone Flight Test Operations. You will own full budget development and P&L management for the FOS organization, aligning operational capacity, workforce phasing, and lifecycle supportability with planned sales pipelines and business opportunities. 

 Responsibilities 

 Organizational Leadership, Capacity Planning & Financial Ownership: 

 
 Organization & Workforce Management: Set operating priorities, build leadership depth, and phase hiring and qualifications against concurrent program needs. 

 
 
 Budget & Lifecycle Cost Ownership: Develop and manage the full departmental budget based on planned sales and business opportunities. Use field, depot, and support case data to assess reliability, maintainability, spares demand, warranty exposure, and total cost of ownership—feeding findings back into repair, replacement, and redesign decisions. 

 
 
 Demand & Capacity Planning: Balance resources and assets against customer demands and the need to provide live fire demonstrations and exercise operations. Advance site evaluation and planned to ensure successful execution. 

 
 
 Contract Execution & Operational Planning: Support the development of Concepts of Operations (CONOPs) for contracted systems. Represent FOS in weekly contract execution meetings, track readiness and fielding actions, and raise risks that could impact contract milestones. 

 Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner tightly with Engineering, Program Management (PMO), Sales, Business Development, Marketing, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain to ensure seamless execution from production through field sustainment. 

 
 Core Functional Areas 

 
 Field System Readiness & Deployment: 

 
 
 Serve as Epirus’s Deployment Coordinator, owning companywide deployment schedules, personnel and equipment movements, rotations, and redeployment across functional teams. 

 
 
 Oversee post-manufacturing system readiness testing and lead pre-deployment site surveys and reviews with customers prior to shipment to validate site readiness and infrastructure requirements. 

 
 
 Field Service & Technical Operations: 

 
 
 The Field service and technical operations teams are composed of field service technicians and technical operations engineers support all customer repairs, system testing, and on-call customer support, 24/7. They also will manage all service depots and remanufacturing process for component level service. 

 
 
 FSR Management & Scheduling: Manage Field Service Representatives (FSRs) technicians, supporting, scheduling, deployment rotations, customer coverage, and training across CONUS and OCONUS operations.

Responsibilities:

The Director, Compliance, Quality & Risk Management provides enterprise-wide strategic and operational leadership for the Foundation’s compliance, organizational quality, and enterprise risk management functions. 
The Director is accountable for establishing and maintaining integrated frameworks, governance processes, and performance standards that strengthen organizational accountability, regulatory compliance, operational effectiveness, and proactive risk management across Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation. The Director owns the enterprise risk management framework, leads enterprise quality improvement and compliance oversight, and partners with executive and operational leaders to identify systemic risks, establish organizational standards, and drive measurable improvements. The Director provides leadership across a complex, multi-state healthcare organization, translating regulatory requirements, organizational risks, and performance insights into actionable strategies that advance the Foundation’s mission, operational integrity, and long-term sustainability.
 
 
This role strengthens Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation’s ability to manage regulatory complexity, maintain consistent quality standards, identify enterprise risks, and provide coordinated oversight across a geographically dispersed organization. Through integrated governance and disciplined execution, the Director helps protect the Foundation’s mission, supports organizational sustainability, and advances the delivery of safe, ethical, high-quality services.

* Enterprise Compliance Leadership
* Quality Management and Continuous Improvement
* Enterprise Risk Management and Patient Safety
* Leadership, Governance and Enterprise Integration

Qualifications:

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business administration, nursing, public health, compliance, risk management, law, or a related field.
* Seven or more years of progressive experience in healthcare compliance, quality management, risk management, patient safety, or related disciplines.
* Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint.
* Three or more years of experience leading teams, programs, or significant cross-functional initiatives.
* Experience managing complex projects and collaborating with executive and operational leaders.
* Demonstrated knowledge of healthcare regulatory frameworks, compliance practices, and quality improvement methodologies.
* Strong analytical, communication, investigation, and problem-solving capabilities.
* Demonstrated sound judgment, professional integrity, and ability to handle sensitive or confidential matters.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Advanced degree in healthcare administration, business administration, public health, law, or a related field.
* Experience in behavioral healthcare, substance use disorder treatment, or a multi-state healthcare organization.
* Experience with Joint Commission or other applicable accreditation standards.
* Knowledge of HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, CMS requirements, and state behavioral health regulations.
* Professional certification such as CHC, CHPC, CPHQ, CPHRM, or equivalent.
* Experience designing enterprise risk frameworks, compliance programs, or integrated quality systems.
* Experience leading organizational transformation or consolidating multiple functions

The Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation is the largest nonprofit addiction recovery organization in the United States. It is also one of the most mission-driven places you will find. The Hazelden Betty Ford Foundation team is passionate about providing hope and ultimately healing. **Why 7 Brew? Because We Invest in YOU!**

At 7 Brew, it’s more than coffee—it’s about brewing smiles one cup at a time. We’re built on kindness, connection, and community, and every guest interaction is an opportunity to make someone’s day brighter.

Brewtopia, a passionate franchise group, is proud to bring the bold energy of 7 Brew to Southeast Michigan. With proven success in quick-service restaurants, we’re dedicated to operational excellence, people-first leadership, and a high-energy drive-thru experience that stands out.

We’re looking for a high-energy, people-first Director of Operations to lead our drive-thru coffee operations. This is a unique opportunity to shape the culture, systems, and guest experience from the ground up—and to grow with us as we expand.

**OUR VALUES**

* Strive for Excellence – We raise the bar every day.
* Elevate Others – We build people up.
* Results Driven – We focus on impact.
* Visionary – We dream big and lead with purpose.
* Exceed Expectations – We go beyond what’s expected.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

* **Competitive Salary:** $125,000 base per year
* **Performance Bonus:** 15% target, tied to KPIs and company performance
* **Comprehensive Benefits:** Health insurance, 401K with competitive match, generous PTO
* **Car Allowance:** Up to $500 /month
* **Cellphone Stipend:** Up to $25 a pay
* **Growth & Learning:** Clear development plans and a culture of continuous improvement
* **More Than Coffee:** Infused energy drinks, Italian sodas, smoothies, teas, and more!

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

The Director of Operations ensures consistency, quality, and efficiency across all locations—protecting the brand and growing guest loyalty. This role optimizes profitability, develops strong leaders, and executes strategic growth initiatives with relentless focus on the guest.

* **Operations & Guest Experience:** Oversee day-to-day operations across multiple drive-thru shops, ensuring speed of service, drink quality, food safety, cleanliness, and brand consistency.
* **Team Leadership & Development:** Lead, mentor, and develop Regional Leaders and General Managers, fostering a culture of accountability, recognition, and continuous growth.
* **Financial Management & Strategic Growth:** Own the P&L, manage labor and COGS, drive sales and flow-through, and collaborate with leadership to execute growth strategies and support new shop openings.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

* **Drive Growth & Profitability:** Regularly review and adjust the budget and financial reports to ensure cost goals are met. Implement strategies to optimize labor, track performance against financial goals, and ensure key profit-driving actions are executed in a timely manner.
* **Ensure Operational Excellence:** Conduct daily operational reviews to ensure adherence to brand standards. Regularly assess performance metrics, respond to customer feedback, and implement action plans to improve service quality.
* **Lead & Develop Teams:** Hold weekly one-on-one coaching sessions with Regional Managers, ensuring consistent training and development. Work with HR and other departments to fill staffing gaps quickly and develop training programs that align with business needs.
* **Foster Guest Satisfaction & Compliance:** Address and resolve guest concerns within 24 hours, ensuring that guest satisfaction is prioritized.
* **Collaborate & Align:** Actively participate in weekly leadership meetings, contribute to discussions, and align team goals with corporate objectives. Share progress updates and ensure all team members are informed and working toward shared priorities.
* **Culture Keeper:** Foster a recognition culture, coach privately and praise publicly, and promote healthy competition and collaboration across locations.

Requirements:

**ESSENTIAL SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS**

* **Leadership & Team Management:** Proven ability to build, coach, and scale high-performing multi-unit teams
* **Financial Acumen:** Budgeting, P&L ownership, l

Description:

**The Company:**

This publicly held clinical-stage biotechnology company is focused on developing treatments for patients suffering from complex rare diseases using its novel cell penetrating peptide technology platform. Their lead product candidate, nomlabofusp, is a subcutaneously administered, recombinant fusion protein intended to deliver human frataxin (FXN), an essential protein to the mitochondria of patients with Friedreich’s ataxia. Friedreich’s ataxia is a rare, progressive, and fatal disease in which patients are unable to produce sufficient FXN due to a genetic abnormality.

The company has 80 employees and has assembled an experienced management team, each of whom has over 20 years of pharmaceutical industry experience. The management team, employees, and consultants have significant expertise in discovery, nonclinical and clinical development, regulatory affairs, commercialization, and the development of manufacturing processes utilizing good manufacturing practices (GMPs).

The company’s strategy is to become a leader in the treatment of rare diseases by leveraging their technology platform and applying their team’s know-how and expertise to the development of CTI-1601 and other future pipeline programs. They are best characterized by entrepreneurial and scientific leadership and a participatory workforce committed to success.

**Position Summary:**

The Director, GxP Vendor Management is responsible for leading Larimar’s GxP vendor management and audit programs and collaborating with key functional area stakeholders to ensure vendors are selected, qualified, managed and overseen in compliance with Larimar and regulatory requirements. This role owns the full vendor lifecycle and will shape the program’s strategy as Larimar seeks BLA approval, progresses with Phase 3 trial and plans for commercialization.

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Lead and implement the strategic direction of the vendor management and audit programs at Larimar.
* Own the risk-based vendor qualification framework, including risk tiering and minimum oversight expectations for each tier, and manage day-to-day qualification activities through vendor audit and assessment, qualification, approval and filing of vendor-related qualification documentation.
* Maintain an approved vendor list and a master tracker of all GxP vendors (current, historic, and planned) as the single source of truth for vendor qualification/requalification, audit, and Quality Agreements.
* Partner with functional areas to develop and oversee execution of the risk-based annual external audit plan, including auditor assignments, audit tracking, follow up of audit responses and CAPAs, and filing of audit documentation.
* Manage the internal audit program including development and execution of internal audit plan to adequately assess Larimar’s internal processes.
* Manage the Quality Agreement program, including development and maintenance of Quality Agreements, and partner with Legal and functional areas to ensure Quality Agreements are in place and current with applicable vendors.
* Partner with functional areas to develop, review and maintain risk-based vendor oversight plans, including expectations for KPIs; governance meetings; issue escalation; oversight activities, frequency, responsibility, and documentation requirements; and verification that vendors and their subcontractors use qualified personnel.
* Conduct training on vendor management and audit programs to ensure functional areas understand and appropriately execute their responsibilities.
* Partner with functional areas to identify vendor deviations to assess issues potentially impacting the vendor qualification status or required oversight.
* Develop Vendor Management metrics, analyze vendor performance and compliance trends, and lead a periodic cross-functional vendor review that feeds into Quality Management Review.
* Ensure inspection readiness in the vendor management function and assist function

Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with the**Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award**, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

At Crème de la Crème, learning comes alive like nowhere else. Our centers are places that never stand still because kids never do. And when you join us, you’ll become part of that magic—making a memorable impact on young learners and their families every day. In our wow-worthy world of learning, your talents will be the catalyst for creating child care experiences you've never imagined. You’ll link arms with other exceptional humans who care as much about helping kids reach their highest potential as you do—and you’ll know that your work matters.

* As the Crème School Director of Education and Quality, you will 
 + Lead and develop teachers to ensure curriculum alignment with best practices, state standards, and the individual needs of children.
 + Facilitate training and implementation of our comprehensive and developmentally appropriate curriculum for early childhood education.
 + Provide transformative leadership in the field of early childhood education, staying informed about current trends, research, and best practices.
 + Develop a culture of continuous learning and professional development while leading the teaching staff.
 + Establish and maintain high-quality standards for early childhood education program
 + Conduct regular assessments, evaluations, and audits to ensure compliance with Crème standards and licensing requirements
 + Provide guidance and support to teaching staff, promoting a positive and collaborative work environment. In partnership with the Executive Director, host professional development programs to enhance educators' skills and knowledge.
 + Cultivate positive relationships with teachers and parents, involving them in their child's education and development.
 + Collaborate with the community to enhance the educational experience and promote your school within the community.
 + Assist as needed in daily school operations, at times including direct supervision of children
 + Apply data-driven insights to assess program effectiveness, implement strategies to address identified areas of improvement, fostering a culture of continuous quality enhancement.
* Qualifications:
* + Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, Education Administration, or a related field. (preferred)
 + Meet state specific credentials / guidelines for the role
 + At least one year leadership experience in early childhood education or a related field
 + Proven understanding of early childhood development, educational best practices, and program administration.
 + Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
 + Outstanding customer service skills, strong organizational skills, and multi-task and handle multiple situations optimally.
 + Proven ability to build and sustain positive relationships with diverse staff, families, and community. Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in education.
 + Physically able to use a computer with basic proficiency, lift a minimum of 40pounds, and work indoors or outdoors.
 + Able to assume postures in low levels to allow physical and visual contact with children, see and hear well enough to keep children safe, and engage in physical activity.
 + Read, write, understand, and speak English to connect with children and their parents in English.

**Our benefits meet you where you are.** We’re here to help our employees navigate the integration of work and life: 

* Know your whole family is supported with **discounted child care** benefits.

*

**Position Summary:**

The Director of Operations is responsible for leading and optimizing all aspects of business unit operations (water, wastewater and natural gas) to achieve exceptional safety performance, operational excellence, customer satisfaction, workforce development, and profitable growth. This role serves as a key member of the leadership team, translating strategic objectives into operational execution while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and innovation. The role develops leaders, drives operational consistency, and champions the company's values while positioning the organization for long-term success.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

* Direct supervision of 3-4 managers and provide leadership in support of subordinate managers within a 90+ employee business.

**Hiring Requirements:**

* Four years Technical/Business Administration degree or equivalent, plus extensive (10+ years) experience in the utility industry or equivalent.
* 5+ years of experience in a leadership position responsible for directing and coordinating staff, subcontractors and consultants, and making organizational decisions.
* Excellent financial, business development, customer interaction, and sales skills, with the ability to manage profit and loss responsibilities.
* Thorough understanding of contract administration, specifications, and applicable laws
* Experience in developing strategic plans, leading initiatives, and managing multiple complex priorities to achieve results within demanding timeframes and budgets.
* Excellent writing and presentation, communication (verbal and written) skills required. Computer proficiency with MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
* Proven track record of excellent customer service, strong interpersonal skills, problem-solving ability, and the capability to engage with prospective customers at the leadership level.
* OSHA 10 General Industry Certification, or ability to obtain during pre-employment (company provided online training).
* Pass pre-employment drug screen and physical.
* Ability to obtain and maintain a valid unrestricted Driver's License.

For more than 40 years, WhiteWater has been managing, operating, and maintaining municipal and private water and wastewater facilities throughout the northeast with pride and professionalism. We are a subsidiary of R.H. White, an award-winning construction services and solutions company, that has been in business since 1923.

WhiteWater was named 2019 Utility of the Year by the New England Water Works Association and is passionately focused on safely performing great work with our people for our clients. Help us fulfill our mission of protecting public health and (the environment) our most precious natural resource - water.

WhiteWater is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer, we encourage all qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

**Regional Director Operations**

**Must Reside in Houston, Austin or San Antonio Area**

**This role is bonus eligible 25% and equity eligible**

**Position Summary**

American Medical Response (AMR) seeks a strategic, results-driven Regional Director of Operations to lead operational excellence, financial performance, and business growth across an assigned region. This leadership position builds a collaborative culture, drives operational excellence, strengthens customer and community partnerships, develops high-performing teams, and ensures quality patient care aligned with organizational objectives. This position oversees 13+ locations and manages multiple direct reports.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic leadership and oversight of regional operations to achieve financial, operational, and organizational objectives.
* Drive revenue growth, profitability, market expansion, and business development initiatives.
* Manage budgets, financial forecasts, profit and loss performance, and operational expenses.
* Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, enhance service delivery, and maximize resources.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with healthcare partners, government agencies, community leaders, and key stakeholders.
* Lead, coach, and develop teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure exceptional customer service, contract performance, and long-term client retention.
* Oversee regulatory compliance, safety standards, emergency preparedness, and company policies.
* Partner with regional and corporate leadership to execute strategic initiatives and organizational priorities.
* Support labor relations, workforce planning, and employee engagement initiatives.
* Champion operational best practices, innovation, and quality patient care.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

**Experience**

* Minimum of five years of progressive management experience, including financial oversight and employee leadership.
* Demonstrated success in operational management, strategic planning, and relationship development.
* Healthcare or emergency medical services industry experience is strongly preferred.
* Air Medical Industry experience is highly preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Strong business and financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, and profit and loss management.
* Proven ability to lead teams, execute strategic initiatives, and deliver measurable business results.
* Excellent communication, interpersonal, negotiation, and decision-making skills.
* Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
* Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
* Knowledge of healthcare operations, regulatory requirements, and clinical practices preferred.
* Ability to travel approximately 50% within assigned areas as needed.
* Must meet AMR's driving and insurability requirements.

Global Medical Response (GMR) and its family of solutions are dedicated to delivering compassionate, quality medical care, primarily in the areas of emergency and patient relocation services. GMR’s Core Behaviors—keep care at the center, raise your hand, seek to understand, find a way together and be accountable—unite our teams and set us apart in emergency medical services.

Job Summary

The Director of Compliance provides strategic and operational leadership for critical compliance activities across the medical device organization. This role leads regulatory inspection readiness, product issue escalation and compliance risk assessment, regulatory agency responses, correction and removal activities, and large-scale compliance improvement initiatives.
 
 
The Director serves as a senior compliance partner to Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Medical Safety, Operations, R&D, Supply Chain, and business leadership, ensuring significant quality and compliance issues are rapidly assessed, appropriately escalated, and effectively resolved. The position requires strong judgment, executive communication, and the ability to lead complex, cross-functional activities in a highly regulated environment.
 
 
Beyond compliance subject-matter leadership, the Director owns the compliance function's budget and resourcing, shapes its organizational strategy and structure, and contributes to broader business planning — balancing business objectives with compliance risk and representing the function in strategic and operational business reviews. The Director leads a global team of regional compliance specialists, building organizational capability across all manufacturing sites and functions.



**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

Organizational Strategy & Business Leadership

* Shape the multi-year strategy and organizational design for the compliance function, including workforce planning, capability building, and succession planning.

* Lead, develop, and manage a global team of compliance professionals, including direct oversight of regional compliance specialists across manufacturing sites.

* Partner with business, Quality, and Regulatory leadership to align compliance priorities with broader business strategy, product roadmaps, and operational plans.

* Represent the compliance organization in business planning, budget reviews, and strategic planning forums, providing a compliance-risk perspective to business decisions.

* Build organizational capability and structure to scale the compliance function as the business grows.

Inspection Readiness

* Establish and maintain an enterprise inspection-readiness program supporting regulatory inspections and other external assessments.

* Lead inspection preparation, including readiness assessments, mock inspections, documentation reviews, front-room/back-room preparation, subject-matter-expert coaching, and inspection logistics.

* Identify systemic readiness gaps and drive corrective actions to improve sustained inspection preparedness.

* Develop inspection-readiness metrics, lessons learned, and continuous-improvement mechanisms.

Product Issue Escalation & Risk Assessment

* Lead or facilitate cross-functional assessments of significant product quality, safety, compliance, and regulatory issues requiring senior-level escalation.

* Ensure emerging product issues are evaluated using structured, documented risk-based decision-making.

* Partner with Medical Safety, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Engineering, Operations, and other functions to evaluate product and compliance risk and determine appropriate escalation and response.

* Provide independent compliance challenge and guidance when significant product-related decisions could create regulatory or patient-safety implications.

* Ensure escalated issues have clear ownership, documented rationale, timely decisions, and appropriate executive visibility.

Regulatory Agency Responses

* Lead the development and coordination of responses to regulatory inspection observations, agency inquiries, compliance correspondence, and other significant regulatory matters.

* Establish cross-functional response teams, governance, deliverables, and escalation mechanisms.

* Ensure responses are factually supported, internally consistent, appropriately reviewed, and supported by sustainable corrective actions.

McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

**About the Role**
------------------

The Director, Revenue Cycle Management provides strategic leadership across key Revenue Cycle functions, including outsourced operations and vendor management, credit balance management, and quality assurance. This role is accountable for improving financial and operational performance, strengthening controls, and ensuring internal teams and external partners consistently meet established service, quality, and compliance expectations.

 
 

You will partner across Revenue Cycle, Finance, Compliance, Operations, IT, and Training to improve cash and accounts receivable performance, resolve operational risks, and drive standardized, sustainable processes. This role provides leadership across multiple teams, vendors, and functional areas and translates organizational strategy into measurable operational goals and results.

 
 

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Lead Revenue Cycle operations and strategic support functions across areas such as patient access, business office operations, claims, accounts receivable, registration, insurance verification, payment and adjustment activities, and customer service.
* Provide governance and performance oversight for **third-party and BPO vendors**, including service-level agreements (SLAs), key performance indicators (KPIs), productivity, quality, contractual performance, issue escalation, and remediation.
* Lead **credit balance operations**, including identification, validation, refunds, adjustments, aging, resolution, root-cause analysis, and prevention of recurring patient and payer credit balances.
* Lead the **Revenue Cycle Quality Assurance program**, including quality standards, audit methodologies, sampling, scoring, performance reporting, corrective action plans, controls, and ongoing monitoring.
* Drive financial and operational performance across assigned Revenue Cycle functions, including cash, accounts receivable, operating expense, vendor spend, quality, compliance, customer experience, and productivity.
* Partner with Revenue Cycle, Finance, Compliance, Operations, IT, Training, and external vendors to identify operational risks, resolve complex issues, standardize processes, and execute continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish governance, reporting, and escalation processes that identify performance gaps and support accountability, risk mitigation, root-cause analysis, and measurable improvement.

*Other duties may be assigned as needed to meet Company goals.*

 
 

**Basic Requirements**
----------------------

* **Degree or equivalent experience. Typically requires 12+ years of professional experience and 4+ years of management experience.**
* Demonstrated professional experience in **Revenue Cycle Management or Revenue Cycle Operations**, including accounts receivable or related healthcare financial operations.
* Experience leading **third-party vendors, outsourced operations, or Business Process Outsourcing (BPO)** relationships, including vendor performance, SLAs, KPIs, or contract performance.
* Experience with **credit balance management**, including refunds, adjustments, resolution, aging, or related accounts receivable processes.
* Experience with **Revenue Cycle quality assurance, auditing, controls, or performance improvement**.

Cenveo is a leading North American manufacturer of envelopes with over 100 years of experience and approximately 30 billion envelopes manufactured annually. We are committed to safety, quality, and operational excellence.

We are hiring immediately for an experienced Plant Manager for its envelope manufacturing facility in Chicago, IL. The position will report into the Site-Leader/General Manager.

Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, Cenveo provides competitive pay and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Job Summary**

The Plant Manager directs the manufacturing, maintenance, warehousing and distribution operations of a facility to achieve business goals including safety, quality, and production (including efficiency and profitability). They ensure compliance with all government regulations and corporate policies. Additionally, the Plant Manager serves as a liaison between the manufacturing facility and its clients, the Sales department, and other groups.

**Key Responsibilities** (\*Essential Functions)

*These are functions a qualified incumbent or applicant must be able to perform with or without reasonable accommodation.*

* Through direct action and the management of others, ensure the safe, productive, and profitable daily operations of an envelope manufacturing facility.
* Effectively use financial, & other, reports to monitor and improve facility performance on a variety of business related metrics. Prepare similar reports as required.
* Select, train, and develop subordinates necessary to conduct facility operations.
* Direct the plant supervision team in the enforcement and consistent application of policies, and plant rules which may include the terms of a collective bargaining agreement.
* Monitor, train and communicate safety and quality programs and ensure compliance with company policies and government regulations.
* Ensure the efficient and effective purchasing and utilization of all materials and services.
* Collaborate with sales to improve or modify existing products as needed, and to aid in new product development.
* Visit customer facilities, or host customer visits to the Cenveo facility to aid in sales, customer relations, or the resolution of problem situations.
* Monitor new trends and developments in business and manufacturing.
* Represent the company and facility in community relations functions.
* Performs other duties as assigned.
* Perform other duties as assigned based on business needs.

**Pay / Other**

* Salaried Pay Range: $120,000 – 140,000 annually
* Schedule: Monday – Friday; Saturdays required during peak production/business needs.

**Other (Non-Essential) Functions**

Includes functions which are normally performed by persons holding this title. However, these functions may be reassigned to other employees as part of a "Reasonable Accommodation" under the ADA.

* Other duties and assignments as required.

**Job Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree preferred. Will consider experience in lieu of Bachelor's degree, emphasis on Manufacturing, Industrial Management, or similar preferred.
* Comprehensive experience in manufacturing, along with advanced knowledge in multiple related disciplines and processes is required.
* Experience in envelope, printing or packaging is highly preferred.
* Extensive experience Environmental, Health, & Safety.
* Six Sigma / Lean Manufacturing experience preferred.
* Managing teams or projects is preferred.
* Strong PC skills including Microsoft Office and internet research
* Strong interpersonal verbal and written communication
* Ability to work independently and with others, demonstrate analytical abilities, and be a strong and versatile leader.
* Must be a self-starter and thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
* Ability to perform work, and resolve problems, that are complex and varied in nature.

* Requires the ability to move throughout a manufacturing facility on a regular basis, incl

**Position Summary**
--------------------

The Director, Quality is responsible for leading multiple manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality resources in the execution of the overall STERIS Quality System. This position is principally responsible for manufacturing/service site or functional quality system execution to drive product/service quality improvement and ensure compliance with, as appropriate, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, MDSAP, FDA QMSR CFR Part 820/211, EU MDR, and other applicable standards. Supporting the GI Reprocessing business, this role provides quality leadership for products, processes, and services that help healthcare providers safely clean, disinfect, and reprocess gastrointestinal endoscopes and related equipment. The Director will champion a culture of quality, compliance, and continuous improvement, helping ensure the delivery of safe, effective, and reliable solutions that support infection prevention, patient safety, and customer confidence. The Quality Director will lead teams of quality managers and engineers responsible for product and service quality, supplier quality, new product/service support, continuous improvement initiatives, and quality system execution. This leader will partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and Commercial teams to drive operational excellence, mitigate risk, support innovation, and enhance quality performance across the GI Reprocessing portfolio.

Preferred onsite location: Mentor, OH, with consideration for candidates based in Plymouth, MN or Conroe, TX.

----------------------------------------

 + Ensures site level compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
 + Drives strategies and methods to continuously improve capital, consumable and service product quality performance.
 + Establishes clear and consistent quality measurement systems in order to monitor and drive results.
 + Leads quality planning and the execution of assigned New Product/Service Development (NPD) projects to achieve targeted quality deliverable adherence.
 + Drives targeted supplier quality improvement efforts and oversees supplier evaluation, approval, and control for assigned manufacturing sites.
 + Assists in the continuous improvement and standardization of quality system procedures and monitor effectiveness.
 + Supports the reliability function by integrating design for reliability tools and techniques within the local projects.
 + Leads quality planning efforts through cross-functional teaming at a site level.
* Supports the New Product/Service Development process and projects to ensure projects attain cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
* Directs local staff on planning sequential and concurrent quality activities. Establish planning and monitoring tools and techniques.
* Provides Quality viewpoints and opinions in planning and specifying existing and future products.
* Assists in the development of the Quality budget. Helps to ensures resources are adequate to fully support the Quality System.
* Takes ownership of all local quality issues, projects, and development activities. Works closely with the site’s Senior Management Teams to provide strategic direction and development of the manufacturing sites product quality strategies and tactics.
* Manages and provide direction to a teams of quality professionals both at corporate and manufacturing sites, with responsibility for hiring, performance management, appropriate staffing, and deployment of resources.
* Assures that local sites maintain and improve operational and quality systems to remain in a state of compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory

* Monitor deployment progress, performance metrics, and organizational adoption to ensure successful execution and sustainment.

* Bachelor's Degree and 10+ years of experience in Quality, Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Program Management, or a related field; or an Advanced Degree and 7+ years of relevant experience.
* Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives, technology deployments, or business transformation activities.
* Strong knowledge of GD&T (ASME Y14.5), 3D model-based engineering practices, and manufacturing quality req

Duties Description Kirby Forensic Psychiatric Center (KFPC), an Office of Mental Health (OMH) secure forensic facility, is recruiting a Deputy Director, Psychiatric Center 1 - Quality Management (DDPC 1 - QM) to oversee their Quality Management Program.
 
 
The DDPC 1 - QM is an essential member of the facility's Executive Management Team. Under the general direction of the Executive Director and in close collaboration with the facility leadership team at KFPC, the DDPC 1 – QM participates in developing, implementing, interpreting, and evaluating the facility's mission, goals, and policies and how they impact the care and clinical treatment provided to the adults, youth, and families they serve.
 
 
The DDPC 1 – QM is responsible for:
 

* Supervising all departments assigned to the Quality Management Program - program evaluation, risk management, utilization review, health information management, and staff development.
* Ensuring compliance with OMH, The Joint Commission (TJC), the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), and external regulatory agencies standards, cultural competence, and continuous quality improvement.
* Ensuring high-quality and effective care in both inpatient and outpatient programs.

Minimum Qualifications Minimum Qualifications:
 
 
A. Education
 
 
A master’s degree in a mental hygiene discipline, hospital or health administration, or other administrative area specifically related to health care, sociology, statistics, or quantitative research; or a license to practice medicine in New York State or Canada.
 
 
AND
 
 
B. Experience
 
 
Six (6) years of experience in a mental health program or health care setting that includes one of the following:
 
 
1. Four (4) years of managerial experience in one quality management component area, such as program evaluation, clinical risk management, standards compliance, survey readiness, utilization review, or a closely related area; or
 
2. Three (3) years of managerial experience in two of the above quality management component areas; or
 
3. Two (2) years of managerial experience in three of the above quality management component areas.

Additional Comments About KFPC
 
KFPC, located on Ward’s Island in New York City, provides inpatient treatment and rehabilitation to pretrial defendants who were deemed unfit to stand trial and were court ordered for restoration of fitness to stand trial and individuals who have been found not guilty by reason of insanity.
 
 
KFPC is committed to supporting underserved individuals and delivering treatment with respect for each individual's privacy and rights along with activities and initiatives to reduce disparities in access, quality, and treatment for underserved populations.
 
 
About OMH
 
OMH operates the largest state mental health system in the country, with 23 hospitals, 90 clinics, two world-class research institutes, a secure residential center, and a network of community services. OMH hospitals are all Joint Commission-accredited and recognized as among the best mental health hospital systems in the United States. OMH believes everyone should have an equal opportunity to achieve mental wellness. This means implementing services and policies to reduce disparities in access, quality, and treatment outcomes for historically marginalized, underserved, and unserved populations.
 
 
If you would like to join KFPC and contribute to a workforce dedicated to public service, we offer:
 

* Generous paid time off, including thirteen (13) vacation days, eight (8) sick days, and five (5) personal days accrued during the first year of employment; thirteen (13) paid holidays each year.
* Option to choose a NYS health insurance plan that meets your needs.
* Dental and vision coverage.
* Enrollment in the New York State and Local Retirement System (NYSLRS) or a voluntary defined contribution plan.

 
The posted salary includes the Downstate Adjustment of $4,150.
 
 
#LI-DNI

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman’s Defense Systems is looking for a **Director Mission Assurance 1** to lead the Quality and Mission Assurance organization for the Strategic Deterrent Systems Division. This leadership role is located in **Roy, Utah**. This role requires strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills to lead in a dynamic engineering and production environment. There is significant responsibility and visibility with executive leadership and the broad customer organization.

**What You'll Get To Do:**

* Defines and monitors mission assurance program specifications and processes to ensure mission success of programs.
* Performs or assures quality, risk management, safety, reliability and maintainability of program achievements, subcontractors, and suppliers in accordance with contractual requirements.
* Assesses program performance and risks and determines resources to ensure mission assurance.
* Ensures the on-time delivery of high-quality products and services that meet all contractual requirements and business objectives.
* Drives the continuous improvement of people (to include training & development), products, processes, systems and services through the application of world class manufacturing to include innovative technologies, lean principles, six-sigma projects, and common best practices.
* Develops, maintains, and ensures compliance with mission assurance programs, policies, processes, procedures and that the performance and quality of products/processes conform to established standards, specifications and agency guidelines.
* Provides expertise and guidance in interpreting policies, regulatory and/or governmental regulations, and agency guidelines to assure compliance.
* Provides leadership that fosters an inclusive, motivated and engaged work culture.
* Supports the development phase of programs by assuring engineering products and processes conform to internal and customer requirements.
* Works directly with operating entities such as engineering and manufacturing to ensure that inspections, process control analyses and audits are conducted on a continuing basis to enforce requirements and compliance.
* Ensures the Quality/Mission Assurance, Manufacturing, and Engineering processes are consistent with industry capability maturity models and QMS standards (AS9100).
* Provides direct oversight in all efforts related to factory accountability and foreign object elimination practices.
* Reviews trend metrics and analyze misses in order to implement the appropriate improvements to improve performance.
* Standardizes and facilitate root cause / corrective action efforts to resolve quality issues.

* Medical, Dental & Vision coverage
* 401k
* Educational Assistance
* Life Insurance
* Employee Assistance Programs & Work/Life Solutions
* Paid Time Off
* Health & Wellness Resources
* Employee Discounts

record.ROLE_TEXT:
This position will oversee production to enable plant productivity and maintenance and the delivery of quality products to customers in an efficient manner, performs various manual tasks in the pits as required. Production activities and coordinates projects. Maintains quality control and ensures the project is going smoothly and according to schedule.

**Essentials Functions**

* Full and complete working knowledge and understanding of all equipment.
* Promotes and supports safety culture and ensures compliance with safety rules and regulations.
* Manages the plant’s production function while maintaining working relationships with other departments to ensure smooth operation.
* Reviews sales forecast and schedules production to ascertain and meet production quantity and quality requirements.
* Review production and operating reports, and resolve operational, manufacturing, and maintenance problems to ensure safety, while minimizing costs and preventing operational delays.
* Complies, stores, and retrieves production data. Monitors physical inventory levels.
* Oversee employee training requirements.
* Additional major functions include planning, annual budgeting and monthly forecasting, reporting of department’s effectiveness, safeguarding assets, and environmental compliance.
* This position requires knowledge equivalent to that which normally would be acquired through a bachelor’s degree in mechanical, industrial, or chemical engineering, or related field.
* Ability to analyze, troubleshoot, critically think about, and resolve problems with field equipment.
* Make sure all equipment is mechanically sound, safe, and ready to work daily.
* Oversee the daily construction activities at work site, including scheduling of workers, delivery of equipment and materials and progress of the project.
* Professionally and positively motivate and direct activities of the crew to enable the completion of work in a safe environmentally responsible and timely manner.
* Daily pre-job preparation and organization for self and crew members, including safety meetings.
* Complete and turn in all paperwork and log in a professional, legible, and timely manner.
* Manage aggregate production to ensure goals and objectives are met.
* Responsible for maintenance and repair of all mobile and stationary equipment.
* Ensures that the workforce complies with policies, procedures, and regulations to produce a productive labor climate at plant facilities.
* Assist Plant Managers and Quality Control Departments as necessary to ensure quality products, accounts & service.
* Assist in development of riverbed aggregate sites, pit operations and reclamation.
* Equipment repair and preventative maintenance
* Interact with vendors and employees.
* Maintain a high degree of customers satisfaction and employee morale through problem solving.
* Ensure a safe working environment through daily inspections and monthly safety meetings.
* Supervise 1-2 aggregate plants (both fixed and mobile)

**Qualifications**

* High School diploma or equivalent
* A minimum of 5 years’ experience in the operations of a sand and gravel pit.
* Experience in a supervisory capacity
* Knowledge of MSHA rules and regulations
* Experience in planning, design, and project management
* Minimum of two years of operating experience
* Ability to understand and follow instructions.
* Ability to learn the methods and practices used in our business.
* Ability to perform strenuous work in varying weather conditions.
* Knowledge of heavy equipment including but not limited to loaders, dozers, and hydraulic excavators and off-road haul trucks. Plant processing includes, but is not limited to water pumps, generators, electrical control components, vibratory screens, sand screws, conveyors, radial stackers, material washers, scales, settling basins, vibratory feeders, and log washers.
* Ability to meet deadlines and multi-task.

**Physical Demands & Work Environment**

Must be able to walk on uneven terra
